conventions: מֵעַל and מֵאַחֲרֵי rendered by a single *from*: מִן takes the *from* and the second preposition is its own `unrepresented` unit (rules 2, 40), the suffix taking its pronoun. Not fused under rule 30, because the ablative *from* carries only the מִן's sense and drops the עַל's or אַחַר's, which is rule 35's test. Corpus: 43 units mark a preposition after מִן `unrepresented` and 155 align מִן to *from* before another preposition; but the corpus fuses מֵאֵת → *from* into one unit in ~20–44, so this is a chapter decision and not a general rule. Where the ASV writes a word for the second preposition (*from off*, *from pursuing*, *above*) that preposition takes it. Applies at 14.5, 14.6 (twice), 14.7, 14.11.

בְּתוֹכָהּ → *in it* / *were in it*: בְּ + תָוֶךְ are one fused unit under rule 30's one-English-word condition, headed on תָוֶךְ, which carries the lexeme; the suffix takes *it* separately, and in the verbless clauses of 14.16, 14.18 and 14.20 the construction-supplied copula *were* joins the fused unit under rule 49, as לִפְנֵי → *was before* does. In 14.14 the written הָיוּ takes *were* and the fused unit holds only *in*. Contrast מִתּוֹךְ עַמִּי at 14.8 and 14.9, where the ASV writes *the midst* and each morpheme has an English word of its own, so rule 2 splits them.

A phrase whose demonstrative or possessive supplies the ASV's single determiner leaves its article morphemes `unrepresented`: הָאֲנָשִׁים הָאֵלֶּה → *these men*, הָאִישׁ הַהוּא → *that man*, הָאָרֶץ הַהִיא → *that land*, and שְׁפָטַי הָרָעִים → *my … sore judgments*. The written demonstrative pronoun or suffix licenses the determiner (rule 41's limit) and the agreement article takes nothing (rules 29, 47). This is the whole of the Td×16 BSB disagreement. Applies at 14.3, 14.8, 14.9, 14.14, 14.16, 14.17, 14.18, 14.19, 14.21.

Supplied subordinators and connectives are counted against the clause's conjunctions (rule 55). Where כִּי or a waw stands it takes the ASV's word — כִּי → *if* (14.9), *when* (14.13, 14.21, 14.23), *but* (14.18); waw → *though* (14.14, 14.18, 14.20), *but* (14.16), *so that* (14.17), *but that* (14.11), *that* recasting a clause as relative (14.7). Where the clause writes no conjunction at all the word is its own `added` unit: *though* at 14.16 (the verse opens with the bare numeral), *if* at 14.17 and 14.19 (the only conjunction is אוֹ, which already has its *Or*), and the restrictive *but* at 14.14 and 14.20. Those five plus the supplied *unto him* of 14.10 are the chapter's six `added` units.

The oath correlatives → *neither … nor*: the opening word goes to the morpheme that is itself what it says — the oath אִם (14.16, 14.20) or the written לֹא (14.18) — and the closing *nor* goes to the waw where one stands (14.16, 14.18) and to the second אִם where none does (14.20). A second אִם standing beside a waw that has taken the *nor* is `unrepresented` under rule 22 (14.16). Read which morphemes are written before placing the pair, as rule 14 directs.

אֲדֹנָי יְהוֹה → *the Lord Jehovah*: no article morpheme stands, so the supplied *the* belongs to the nominal expression אֲדֹנָי determines (rule 15), and the 1cs suffix is `unrepresented` because the ASV writes no *my* (rule 22). Eight verses, and the whole of the Sp1cs×9 BSB disagreement.
report: Checked all 51 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end, since the table is keyed by source lemma and cannot see the chapter's six `added` units — which is where a chapter this full of supplied connectives would hide a split. Every difference the table flags is licensed by what the ASV wrote or by which morpheme stands in the clause, so patches is empty.

Evidence round answered all three requests and confirms the accepted reading of מֵעַל / מֵאַחֲרֵי → *from …*: מִן takes *from*, the second preposition is `unrepresented` (14.5, 14.6 twice, 14.7, 14.11). Corpus: 43 units of עַל after a preposition marked `unrepresented`, several carrying this chapter's own note, and 155 units aligning מִן to *from* before another preposition. LEMMA=אַחַר PREV=R returned 21 units, all aligned, but every one is a place where the ASV spent a word on אַחַר (*following*, *behind*, *from pursuing*, *departing*); none is a case where the ASV wrote only *from*, so none contradicts 14.7 or 14.11.

No promotion or amendment offered. The obvious candidate — a general rule for מִן plus a second preposition rendered by one ablative word — is contradicted by the corpus itself: מֵעַל → *from* splits (43 unrepresented עַל) while מֵאֵת → *from* fuses into one R+R unit in roughly 20–44 units under LEMMA=מִן and LEMMA=אֵת. A corpus that contradicts itself is a reason not to promote, so this is recorded as a chapter convention instead.

BSB: no genuine error. R×15, Td×16 and Sp1cs×9 are the documented convention differences — prepositions silenced by the ASV's recasting (rules 27, 40), articles left unrepresented where the ASV writes one determiner licensed by a demonstrative or a suffix (rule 41's limit), and the 1cs suffix of אֲדֹנָי (rule 22). The two singletons stand: the suffix of כֻּלָּם at 14.5 has no *of them* to take, and the second oath אִם at 14.16 is unrepresented because the waw standing beside it took the *nor* (rule 14).

Checked hard and left alone: the head of הֲשִׂמֹתִיהוּ → *will make him an astonishment* (14.8) stays on *make*. Rule 44's subtraction runs on the source lexeme, and MACULA's lemma is שׂים, which *make* realizes — unlike הִמְלִיךְ → *make king*, where the lexeme sits in *king*. That agrees with 14.11 (*go astray* headed on *astray*) and 14.15 (*cause to pass* headed on *pass*), so the chapter heads every light-verb rendering on the token carrying the source lemma.

Also left alone: the chapter's one `noncompositional` unit, לְבַדָּם → *only* at 14.16, beside an `aligned` לְבַד → *only* at 14.18 where the ASV writes *themselves* for the suffix. The token sets differ and the corpus uses both statuses for the same fusions at scale (לִפְנֵי: 226 noncompositional, 154 aligned), so flattening it would impose a distinction the corpus does not make. Recorded in the conventions instead.
Six conventions recorded. The chapter had none logged against 98 repeated notes, so a verse aligned from the log alone would have had to rediscover all of them.
